extracted.intended_audience: writers and story-tellers interested in screenwriting and story craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers on the principles of screenwriting and storytelling, focusing on substance, structure, style, genre use, and character development. Useful for prose writers, playwrights, and aspiring screenwriters seeking craft principles rather than formulaic models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles over paradigms / avoid 'foolproof' models
rubrics_metrics.description: All notions of paradigms and 'foolproof' story models for commercial success are meaningless. Instead of looking for shortcuts we need to be faithful to our principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute rigid formulas or paradigms for underlying storytelling principles. Focus on understanding and applying principles rather than searching for a shortcut to commercial success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use genre and subgenre systems to inspire, not inhibit
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres don't inhibit creativity – they inspire it and anyone who ever tells a story is really doing so within the principles, structure and style of a genre - even those who rebel against genres!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the genre and subgenre you are working in and use their conventions as creative constraints and inspiration. Recognize that even apparent genre-rebels operate within genre principles, structure, and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize substance, structure and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Story: Substance, structure, style and the principles of screenwriting (the book's core focus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to the three pillars — what the story is about (substance), how it is put together (structure), and how it is expressed (style). These are the foundation for effective screenwriting and storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: observable qualities vs true character
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization is described as the sum of all the observable qualities that make the character unique – but true 'character' is what waits behind this mask to surprise us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop both surface-level observable traits and an inner life that can produce surprising behaviour; avoid equating characterization solely with mannerisms or description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal character through choices under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: True character is revealed through the choices made under pressure – and the greater the pressure, the deeper the revelation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create situations that force characters to make hard choices; escalate pressure/conflict to disclose deeper aspects of personality and produce memorable character moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probe character by testing the opposite choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Having analysed the clear and obvious choice for a character, we then ask what would be the opposite to that and why they would act in that way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After establishing an obvious or expected choice for a character, explicitly consider the antithetical choice and the believable motivations that would lead to it—this generates complexity and surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study many examples across genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Story has hundreds of examples from movies of every genre (the list at the back takes 33 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn craft by studying many film examples across genres; watch films knowing who wrote the story and analyze how principles, structure, and character work in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily writing discipline and willingness to risk rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Find someone who was prepared to write every day, line by line, page by page – with the courage to risk rejection and failure in the quest for stories told with real meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a habit of regular writing and accept rejection as part of the process; persistence and daily practice are central to producing work with depth and meaning.
